investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods stuck unscheduled for 141–147 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. Because no VM slot could be allocated, the agent pod never started, the remote agent never reached a ready state, and the eval runner received no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to satisfy the expected-output contract. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint failure in the production Kubernetes environment, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable slots for new pods. No preemption victims exist, so the scheduler cannot free capacity automatically.

Secondary: The node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity. If the selector were broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling would succeed.

Tertiary: A quota or limit range applied at the namespace or org level may be capping the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm units available to the eval probe's service account, causing apparent exhaustion even if raw node capacity exists.

Lower probability: A node that previously carried kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was cordoned, drained, or removed from the cluster, reducing the pool from a larger number to 2 nodes and tipping the cluster into a capacity-exhausted state.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods stuck unscheduled for 141–147 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. Because no VM slot could be allocated, the agent pod never started, the remote agent never reached a ready state, and the eval runner received no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to satisfy the expected-output contract. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint failure in the production Kubernetes environment, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable slots for new pods. No preemption victims exist, so the scheduler cannot free capacity automatically.

Tertiary: A quota or limit range applied at the namespace or org level may be capping the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm units available to the eval probe's service account, causing apparent exhaustion even if raw node capacity exists.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-04 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no response evidence whatsoever — all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote agent pod times out unscheduled (~141–150 s), preventing any agent lifecycle step from starting. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-facing production incident is present; the impact is localized to the AURA observability eval suite for the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment.

This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, expanding the eligible node pool could resolve scheduling even without adding VM quota.

Tertiary — a concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if previous eval runs or user workloads did not release their VM resources, the quota could be artificially depleted. The eval runner uses withCleanup (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1916), but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned pods holding VM slots.

Lower probability — the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota was recently reduced or the node pool was scaled down, shrinking available capacity below the level needed to schedule even a single eval pod. No source evidence confirms a quota or node-count change.
